sets.title: PSM II Advanced Situational Practice Assessment Set 1
sets.description: Full-length 30-scenario PSM II exam simulation. 90 minutes time limit. 85% passing threshold. Features partial-credit option weighting and domain recommendations.

questions.scenario: [Scenario 1] [Organizational Agility & Leadership Coaching] A functional manager attempts to override the Scrum Master by assigning individual daily tasks to Developers during the Sprint, arguing that 'engineers need strict line-management supervision to stay productive.' How should the Scrum Master coach the organization? (Set 1 Context Variation)

options.text: Coach the functional manager on Scrum principles: Developers self-manage their work inside the Sprint; line management intervention destroys accountability and empiricism.
Accept the manager's tasks and add them into the Sprint Backlog without informing the team.
Tell the Developers to work 80 hours a week to complete both the manager's tasks and the Sprint Goal.
Facilitate a session between leadership and the Scrum Team to transition traditional task assignment into outcome-based Sprint Goal alignment.

questions.explanation: Option A (Weight 1.0) reinforces servant leadership by protecting team self-management. Option D (Weight 0.85) is an effective collaborative facilitation step.

recommendation.linkText: Explore Knowledge Hub: Agile Principles & Organizational Coaching
recommendation.action: Study techniques for shifting enterprise leadership from predictive Gantt charts to empirical outcome governance.

questions.scenario: [Scenario 2] [Product Owner Mentorship & Value Maximization] A Product Owner is being pressured by five powerful business executives, each demanding their specific feature be built first. The Product Owner is overwhelmed and agrees to all requests, creating an un-ordered backlog of 200 items. What is the Scrum Master's best coaching response? (Set 1 Context Variation)

options.text: Take over Product Backlog management completely and order items based on technical complexity.
Coach the Product Owner on defining a clear Product Goal and using empirical value techniques (e.g. WSJF, ROI, cost of delay) to confidently say 'no' to low-value demands.
Tell the Developers to build all 200 items in parallel across the next two Sprints.
Facilitate a joint stakeholder alignment workshop to help the Product Owner establish transparent value criteria and ordering consensus.

questions.explanation: Option B (Weight 1.0) mentors the Product Owner on value maximization and Product Goal clarity. Option D (Weight 0.8) supports stakeholder collaboration.

recommendation.topic: Product Backlog Management & Product Goal Formulation
recommendation.linkText: Visit Tools Hub: Jira & Backlog Management Guides
recommendation.action: Learn value-based backlog ordering, user story slicing, and effective stakeholder boundary management.

questions.scenario: [Scenario 3] [Developer Self-Management & Facilitation] Three days into a 2-week Sprint, the Developers discover a major unforeseen technical vulnerability in the core database architecture. Fixing it will require 40% of the Sprint capacity. What should the Scrum Master guide the team to do? (Set 1 Context Variation)

options.text: Guide the Developers to immediately consult with the Product Owner to inspect the impact on the Sprint Goal and re-negotiate scope as needed.
Hide the vulnerability from the Product Owner and fix it secretly in the next release.
Cancel the Sprint immediately without discussing options with the team.
Encourage the Developers to evaluate whether the vulnerability threatens the Increment's Definition of Done and adapt the Sprint Backlog transparently.

questions.explanation: Option A (Weight 1.0) promotes transparency and negotiation between PO and Developers. Option D (Weight 0.9) enforces Definition of Done integrity.

recommendation.linkText: Review Workshop Facilitation & Team Coaching Tools
recommendation.action: Practice facilitating self-managed planning, technical spike negotiations, and peer-to-peer accountability.
